b1.summary: Every run fails the recursive-copy test (T4). In 5 of 6 runs (and per the truncated summary likely also DS run 2's copy failure) the model added a per-child destination scope check, so the victim stays unchanged, but CopyDir's error aggregation (errors.New(errString)) drops os.ErrPermission and errToStatus returns 500 instead of 4xx. The test (zz_sec_scope_test.go:92-93) checks status 4xx before the victim content, so these are contract-only failures: no hole is open. Only DS run 2 has a real security miss: its resolver filepath.Clean-ed an absolute link target with '..' after a symlinked component, so the upload created a file outside the scope.

b4.note: Same copy-route 500-vs-4xx error-mapping failure in all 6 runs; DS run 2 adds one T1 '..'-after-symlink resolver miss.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES, asking only which test decided the 0.8571 runs. qa_runs answers it (the copy test), and the review already judged that test fair including the 5xx-aggregation case ('a stated-requirement violation, not a test artifact').

b6.reason: Copy per-child destination (T4) is unchanged by both published fixes; checks/upstream_fix.patch (A+B) still fails the copy route and both '..'-after-symlink shapes (gate 0.5714; notes.md: 'still follows the copy destination link'). notes.md has one contradictory line ('upstream A+B fix reports a permission error on the copy route'), and present_in_latest is 'unknown'.
